name: cloud-cost-review
description: Review actual cloud spend from a cost export (AWS CUR or Data Exports, GCP billing export, Azure cost details) and produce a ranked savings report — idle and unattached resources, oversized instances backed by utilisation evidence, storage tiering, data transfer hot spots, commitment coverage and untagged spend — each finding with a monthly saving computed from the bill, a confidence level and an ease rating. Use when the user shares a cost CSV and says "where are we wasting money", "review our AWS bill", "why did the cloud bill jump this month", "find savings in our GCP/Azure spend", or "should we buy savings plans".

handoff.when: logging or metrics ingestion is a top cost hot spot
handoff.purpose: Set a telemetry cardinality and log-volume budget that brings the observability line down.
handoff.fallback: If observability-plan is absent, list the top log groups or metric namespaces by cost and propose a retention and sampling cap for each inline.

handoff.when: the user needs the bill projected forward for growth or a launch
handoff.purpose: Model cost from a demand driver at 1×/3×/10×, using this review's actual unit costs.
handoff.fallback: If capacity-cost-model is absent, state the current cost per unit of the main driver and say that a linear projection ignores scaling cliffs.

model.rationale: A stdlib script does the aggregation; the model maps columns, checks evidence and computes savings with shown arithmetic against a fixed category checklist, which is bounded judgment.
